jurisdictions.name: New Orleans (Orleans Parish)
jurisdictions.office: City of New Orleans Department of Safety & Permits
notes: A swimming pool permit is required to build or alter any type of pool in the city. Applications are made online through the One Stop App.

Residential submittals include a plot plan with all lot and structure dimensions and setbacks, a signed contract or estimate, contractor license information, and the Residential Swimming Pool Acknowledgment.
Commercial and public pools need two sets of plans with live seals from a Louisiana licensed architect or civil engineer. The page lists that seal requirement for commercial permits only.

Plan review checks the city's amendments to the International Building Code and its zoning ordinance. Pools in the Vieux Carré need Vieux Carré Commission approval, and other historic districts need Historic Districts Landmark Commission approval.

sources.title: Swimming Pool Permit - City of New Orleans

jurisdictions.name: Baton Rouge (East Baton Rouge Parish)
jurisdictions.office: East Baton Rouge City-Parish Permit & Inspection Division, Department of Development
notes: A residential pool permit needs a site or plot plan showing pool location, dimensions, depth, equipment location, servitudes, and setbacks from property lines, streets, alleys and the house.
The contractor and homeowner must sign a Pool Barrier Affidavit, which can be submitted with the permit application documents. Depths over 5 ft need a secondary entry and exit.
Separate plumbing and electrical permits are required. Electrical inspections cover pool bonding and pool deck bonding before concrete is poured.

Pools in Urban Design Overlay Districts need Planning Commission staff approval. Locally designated historic districts need a Certificate of Appropriateness. The parish does not enforce private subdivision restrictions.

sources.title: Swimming Pool Permit Information and Requirements - East Baton Rouge Department of Development

jurisdictions.name: Mandeville
jurisdictions.office: City of Mandeville Planning and Development
notes: The city says permits are needed so construction complies with the current edition of the Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code.
The city's permit forms include a Swimming Pool Permit application, and applications are submitted digitally by email to the permits office.
That application's checklist asks for a surveyor-certified boundary survey and a fully dimensioned site plan showing setbacks and existing structures.
The same checklist asks for a drainage plan stamped by a Louisiana licensed civil engineer or land surveyor, and an elevation certificate in FEMA flood zones AE or V.

jurisdictions.name: St. Tammany Parish (unincorporated)
jurisdictions.office: St. Tammany Parish Department of Permits and Inspections
notes: The parish's residential pool plan review checklist asks for a property survey showing the flood zone, a pool cross section, and a plot plan with existing and proposed structures, setback lines, the fence location, height and materials, window and door alarm locations, pool equipment and any pool heater.

Under Section 400-8.PP of the parish's Unified Development Code, a pool must be completely enclosed by a permanent, solidly built fence or wall at least 4 feet high, and every gate or door in it needs a self-closing, self-latching device. Portable or accessory pools with less than 18 inches of water depth are exempt.

The same section allows pools only in a side or rear yard. In-ground pools (less than 12 inches above grade), including decking and coping, must be set back at least 5 feet from the side and rear property lines. Above-ground pools must be set back at least 5 feet from the side line and 10 feet from the rear line.

The parish's pool packet says all pools will be inspected for compliance with the 2021 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code (ISPSC). From January 1, 2026, once excavation begins, a pool under construction must be protected by a rigid barrier.

sources.title: Residential Swimming Pool Packet, effective 10.08.2026 (St. Tammany Parish)
